name: Ladakhi Apricot Juice
ingredients: 2-4 tablespoons honey or local raw sugar (adjust to taste)
A pinch of crushed roasted cumin seeds (optional for depth)
instructions: 1. If using dried apricots, soak them in water for at least 3-4 hours; if using fresh, wash and pit them.
2. Place the apricots and their soaking liquid (or fresh water) in a pot and bring to a boil.
3. Reduce heat and simmer until the apricots are very soft and can be easily mashed.
4. Remove from heat and allow the mixture to cool to room temperature.
5. Blend the mixture until smooth and strain if a thinner consistency is desired.
6. Stir in the honey, black salt, and optional roasted cumin.
description: Apricots, known as 'Chulli' in Ladakh, are a staple fruit of the region, thriving in its high-altitude, cold-desert climate. This juice is a traditional beverage often offered as a sign of hospitality, celebrated for its cooling properties and rich nutritional value.
